_comment: Everything this skill says that is not a number and not a lesson prompt.
Script only — recording happens separately and is not part of a build phase.
`speaksPrompts: false` is the important line. This skill starts at age 7, and
a child of seven can read. Reading the question aloud to them takes the
reading out of the question — which in a word problem is most of the work — so
no lesson prompt is spoken when a round opens and none is recorded. That is 56
clips this skill does not need.
What it does say is what it says *back* to a child: the reactions, which come
from the common pack and name no subject, and the eighteen refusals below —
the sentence an engine gives when it will not take an answer yet. Those fire
while a child is looking at the tray, not at text, and a tray that refuses a
move in silence reads as broken rather than restrained.
The speaker button stays, unrecorded, on the live TTS path: a child who can do
the division but is stuck on the reading should have a way through, and a
button pressed rarely and on purpose does not need a clip waiting for it.
